sampling_model.design: Four mutually independent repeated-cross-section samples indexed by \(g\in\{C0,C1,T0,T1\}\).
sampling_model.units: Within cell \(g\), \(X_{g,1},\ldots,X_{g,n_g}\) are independent draws from \(P_g\), with \(n=\min_g n_g\) and \(n_g/n\to\rho_g\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment group is untreated at period zero and exposed at period one; the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the no-treatment treated-post map from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell density is bounded between \(c\) and \(C\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), both nested Brenier Jacobians are uniformly elliptic, and the selected population lift branches remain \(\beta\)-separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the order-\(s\) signed periodized KDE followed by clipping at \(c/2\) and mass renormalization. The half-open-cell lift selector returns \(\widehat a_p,\widehat\phi_p,\widehat a_T,\widehat\phi_T\) and uses a fixed measurable fallback off its regular domain. Covariance pilots are two-fold cross-fitted, include the harmonic translation score, and are evaluated by adjoint elliptic solves; \(n^{-1}I_{2J}\) is added before every block inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) only when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).
Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere boundary problem.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual law and map under cyclic comonotonicity, while the estimation section gives consistency rather than a sampling law.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify the gradient-Green contamination influence and its pole singularity; the abstract reports numerical stable-type fluctuations but the paper does not prove a shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.
Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound.
Theorem 18 gives the \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth density plug-in map without a matching logarithmic lower bound.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient influence functions and root-\(n\) cross-fitted inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data.

body.tldr: The intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes functional now has a complete fixed-grid critical inference theory. A uniform local Green parametrix proves that every transformed exact score differs from its frozen-pole response by a bounded \(L^2\) term; moving-pole and coefficient errors are negligible at bandwidth \(h_n\), and the two-dimensional determinant identity yields a uniform quadratic nested remainder. These estimates give the full four-cell covariance, the \(\sqrt{n/L_n}\) Gaussian limit, consistent cross-fitted adjoint covariance, simultaneous multiplier ellipses, and matching squared risk \(L_n/n\).

project_justification.gap: Published transport central-limit results do not prove pointwise gradient inference in dimension two for general variable coefficients with a generated target, and fixed-path differentiability does not control shrinking-bandwidth empirical directions. The note closes this gap by deriving the local variable-coefficient Green expansion, transformed-kernel and moving-pole stability, and a uniform nonlinear moment bound.
project_justification.niche: In the critical plane, each independent cell contributes a positive logarithmic Green variance. Nesting makes both control cells enter directly and through the generated target; the exact pulled-coordinate calculation retains those within-cell cross terms while showing that the remaining composition gains one derivative.
project_justification.fill: The note establishes intrinsic torus identification, the translation-aware nested derivative, an explicit four-cell covariance, a feasible cross-fitted adjoint estimator, fixed-grid multiplier ellipses, and a matched class-uniform upper and fixed-center Hellinger-local lower risk bound. The analytic closure uses a frozen-pole parametrix with an \(O(r^{-1+1/4})\) remainder, second-order coordinate changes, KDE Hölder tails, and the exact two-dimensional determinant identity.

body.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC supplies the multivariate changes-in-changes motivation and Card--Krueger application but stops short of the critical limit law proved here. ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves the dimension-two uniform-law fixed-source case; its general-coefficient freezing bound does not yield the present result. GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization supplies fixed smooth-path differentiability, whereas this note derives shrinking-bandwidth transformed-kernel, moving-pole, and quadratic nested control. GonzalezSanzMordantSheng2026PotentialFCLT treats smoother potential functionals and excludes pointwise gradients. HutterRigollet2021Minimax and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2024Plugin address global one-map risk; the present annular Green alternatives and four-input upper bound establish a distinct fixed-center pointwise logarithmic experiment. PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand concerns one-dimensional quantile-map bands rather than fixed-grid bivariate nested ellipses.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The result is fixed-grid and assumes four independent smooth samples on the flat torus, uniform density positivity, uniform Brenier ellipticity, a fixed lift/cut-locus margin, and the stated polynomial bandwidth window. Numerical Monge--Ampere and adjoint solves must approximate map evaluations, coefficients, and score covariances below their respective statistical scales. The proposed nonseparable \(h,h/2,h/4,h/8\) calculation remains a valuable implementation diagnostic, but is no longer a logical premise of the proof.
body.honest_scope: The proved theorem concerns a balanced four-cell repeated-cross-section experiment with fixed \(J\), smooth positive periodic densities, and translation-aware torus displacements. It does not give a confidence band over \(\mathbb T^2\), allow vanishing densities or degenerating Jacobians, or justify applying the procedure directly to raw discrete or paired Card--Krueger outcomes. A Card--Krueger reanalysis therefore requires a prespecified smooth bivariate periodic outcome construction and a defensible independent-cell sampling approximation, plus numerical tolerances below the stated critical scales.
body.interpretation: At each prespecified treated-post location \(y_j\), the estimand is the translation-aware no-treatment displacement \(y_j-T(y_j)\). The covariance weight \(\alpha(y_j)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})+\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\) shows how uncertainty from all four repeated-cross-section cells contributes. The simultaneous ellipses preserve the direction and covariance of each bivariate arrow while controlling multiplicity across the fixed grid.
